subject: Archaeology
title: Ice Core Dating: Trapped Atmospheres
description: A fast breakdown of Ice Core Dating: Trapped Atmospheres for builders.

hook.text: Air bubbles trapped in Antarctic ice are time capsules of ancient atmospheres — some are 800,000 years old.

buildup.text: Ice sheets build up one layer per year, like tree rings. Drilling down extracts a cylinder of frozen climate history.

discovery.text: Volcanic eruptions leave ash and acid layers in ice. These markers can be matched to known eruptions with exact dates.

twist.text: A mystery volcanic eruption in 536 CE caused a global winter that collapsed civilizations. Ice cores proved it was real.

climax.text: Ice cores confirmed that the Black Death coincided with climate changes — connecting archaeology to climate science.

punchline.text: Eight hundred thousand years of air, frozen in layers.

quiz.question: What did ice cores reveal about the year 536 CE?
options: A massive solar flare disrupted Earth's magnetic field
A mystery volcanic eruption caused a global winter that collapsed civilizations
A comet impact in the Pacific triggered massive tsunamis

details.summary: Ice cores drilled from glaciers and ice sheets contain annual layers of compressed snow trapping ancient air bubbles. These layers record past climate — temperature, atmospheric composition, volcanic eruptions
details.whyItMatters: Ice cores provide the most detailed continuous climate record available. Linking this record to archaeological evidence of human behavior reveals how climate change drove migrations, innovations, and societal collapse across millennia.
takeaways: Annual ice layers trap air bubbles preserving ancient atmosphere
Records extend back 800,000 years of continuous climate data
Climate records contextualize archaeological evidence of human change

faq.question: How do ice cores record annual climate data?
faq.answer: Each year's snowfall compresses into a distinct layer. Summer and winter snow differ in crystal structure and chemistry. Trapped air bubbles preserve atmospheric composition. Volcanic ash layers, dust, and chemical signatures mark specific events. Scientists count layers like tree rings.

faq.question: How deep are ice core drill sites?
faq.answer: The deepest cores from Antarctica reach over 3 kilometers. Each meter of ice represents decades to centuries of accumulation depending on depth. The European EPICA core reaches 800,000 years into the past. Greenland cores provide higher-resolution records for the last 130,000 years.
